fieldMarks: Lanky hare, 47-63 cm long, with very long ears (10-13 cm) and long hind legs.
Black stripe down the centre of the back, a black rump patch, and a tail black on top.
behavior: Mainly nocturnal; rests by day in shallow scraped depressions ('forms') under bushes and is inactive in hot afternoons.
Relies on freezing and speed: flushes in bounds up to 20 ft, reaching 30-35 mph on a zigzag course.
Eats grasses and herbs, turning to twigs, bark, sagebrush and cacti when other food is short; gets most water from plants.
habitat: Desert scrub, prairie, short-grass rangeland, dunes and farmland from sea level to about 3,800 m.
range: Southwestern United States and Mexico, east to Missouri and north to Washington, Idaho, Colorado and Nebraska, west to California and Baja California.

lookalikes.name: White-tailed jackrabbit
lookalikes.howToTell: White-tailed jackrabbit's tail is always white, without the black tail top and back stripe.

lookalikes.name: Eastern cottontail
lookalikes.howToTell: Cottontails are smaller with shorter ears and legs; jackrabbits have ears, hind legs and feet very large in proportion to the body.
